### Shape

#### Description

A multi-line text input whose long lines soft wrap, starting at a single row.

#### Grow To Fit

It grows to fit its text, one row per visual line: both lines broken with <Enter> and long lines that soft wrap, wrapped where it wraps them. It shrinks again as text is removed, and fits again when its width changes, as when the window is resized. Its height is what its rows and their padding and border take, and nothing more: there is no empty row beneath the last line.
Its rows are counted as the input itself lays its text out, in the very font it draws the text in, weight and all, so the count never differs from what shows: while the text is within its most rows, no row is ever cut off or scrolled out of view, and no empty row is left. Should a count made ahead of drawing still differ from how the text was laid out, the input takes the laid out count by the next frame.

#### Most Rows

Whatever uses it says how many rows it grows to at most. Once its text takes more, it stays that tall and scrolls.

#### Steadiness

It grows or shrinks in the very frame its text changes, and at any display scale its height is rounded up to a whole device pixel, so the text never flickers a row up and back as a line is added.
It never takes its height from a frame before. Its rows are counted at the width it is drawn at in this frame, the width its text wraps at, so the first line to wrap adds its row in the frame it wraps, at its final height, with no frame drawn at the old height with the text already wrapped, nor at a height between, nor at a width it then wraps again at. Its height is set once a frame, from that count, never adjusted after the frame is drawn, so it never settles over two or more frames.
The width its text wraps at never depends on whether it scrolls. Its scrollbar, once its text takes more than its most rows, overlays the text's right padding rather than taking width from the text, so reaching its most rows never rewraps the text, never changes its count of rows, and never moves a line from one row to another.

#### Scrolling

Once its text takes more than its most rows, it scrolls only to keep the cursor in view, and then by no more than it takes: typing, pasting, or moving the cursor to a row beneath the last shown scrolls just far enough to show it as the last row, and to a row above the first shown, just far enough to show it as the first. A change of text, its height, or its width that leaves the cursor in view never scrolls it, and a frame never scrolls it to its top and back, nor back and forth between two places. Typing at the end of a long text keeps its last row the last row shown, steadily, keystroke after keystroke. Scrolling it with the wheel or trackpad moves it as far as was scrolled and leaves it there until the cursor moves out of view. Its scroll position is kept in whole device pixels, so its rows never shimmer between two positions.

#### Nothing Else Caps It

It is as tall as its rows need, up to its most rows, wherever it is

content.text:
I fixed both jumps, and measured each one frame by frame before and after. All 527 tests pass, including a new test that types past 12 rows and checks every frame. "Doesn't grow" turned out to be the specified layout, not a bug.

**Jump at the first wrap (and on later wraps):** the height was always right. What jumped was the text: in the first frame after a line wrapped, the editor scrolled it up one row, then snapped back the next frame. That repeated for several keystrokes after each wrap. The cause was the gpui-kit editor keeping a one-row margin between the cursor and the edge of the box. With the box sized exactly to its rows, a cursor on the last row looked too close to the edge, so the editor scrolled. The editor now keeps no margin while the text fits (`cursor_surrounding_lines(Some(0))` in `src/chat_input.rs`).

**Jumping when it gets long:** past 12 rows, scrolling ran a keystroke behind. When row 13 appeared, the cursor sat below the visible area for a keystroke before catching up, and the same happened on later rows. There were two causes, both fixed in `src/growing_input.rs`:
- **Margin switch:** once the text is longer than 12 rows, the editor now keeps a one-row margin, set before it lays out each frame. A new row then scrolls by exactly that row, in the same frame, so the last line stays at the bottom.
- **Cursor out of view:** when a text change leaves the cursor out of view (for example a long paste), it now scrolls just far enough, working out the cursor's row even when that row isn't drawn. Wheel scrolling is left alone.

I checked the scrollbar doesn't narrow the text when it appears, so reaching 12 rows doesn't rewrap anything.

**"Doesn't grow anymore":** it does grow, but only once the text is taller than the button column. In the full layout the dark text box starts 124px tall, because the Send, Queue and Preview buttons beside it are that tall. The text grows inside that box until about the 6th row, and only then does the box grow, row by row, up to 12 rows. That's what the spec asks for: the input row is "as tall as the taller of the text and the buttons". If you want the box to grow from the first wrapped line, the button column would need to be shorter (for example, buttons side by side). That's a spec change.

The spec otherwise matches the prompt.
